newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National interest key to media changes - Australia.
newsitem.headline: National interest key to media changes - Australia.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston, overseeing a review of media ownership controls, said on Wednesday any changes to ownership limits must be in the national interest.

Alston told reporters that publishing and television tycoon Kerry Packer met Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday to discuss Canberra's media ownership review. But he refused to give details of the talks.
"Well I think Mr Packer's views are on the public record and the government's general thinking is also fairly clear," he said.
"So I'm hopeful we'll be able to reach an accommodation in the national interest."
Packer, whose Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) owns the Nine television network and several magazines, also refused to comment on the talks as he left parliament house in Canberra on Tuesday.
PBL owns 11.8 percent of newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and Packer has argued for the end of restrictions preventing major holdings in television and newspapers in the same market.
PBL has said it would like to merge with Fairfax, which is currently 20 percent owned by Brierley Investments Ltd.
The law prevents a television operator owning more than 15 percent of a newspaper in the same market, and vice versa.
Alston said earlier this month that the government could not ignore legitimate commercial reasons for cross media ownership.

He told a Sydney conference on media ownership that many companies saw the need to have interests across the communications sector to achieve economies of scale and bring commercial and technical expertise to new markets.
"These are legitimate competitive efficiency aspirations which should only be curtailed for demonstrable public interest considerations," he said.
